sources.title: Concurrency Response of Plain Global Loads on the NVIDIA H100
sources.snippet: The bandwidth a memory-bound GPU kernel sustains is set by how many bytes it keeps in flight. We use Little's Law here as throughput accounting, not as a measured hardware pool. CUDA fills that budget on Hopper through plain loads (ld.global) and asynchronous copies (cp.async), among other paths; we characterize their concurrency response with clean-room microbenchmarks on three H100 SXM5 dies. sources.title: Story of Two GPUs: Characterizing the Resilience of Hopper H100 and Ampere A100 GPUs
sources.snippet: This study characterizes GPU resilience in Delta, a large-scale AI system that consists of 1,056 A100 and H100 GPUs, with over 1,300 petaflops of peak throughput. We used 2.5 years of operational data (11.7 million GPU hours) on GPU errors.
